newsitem.title: USA: GM stock buyback plan now 88 pct complete.
newsitem.headline: GM stock buyback plan now 88 pct complete.

text.p: General Motors Corp Chief Financial Officer J. Michael Losh said Wednesday the automaker's current $2.5 billion stock repurchase program is now about 88 percent complete.

Losh, speaking to reporters in a conference call, said the additional stock purchases since June 30 had raised the dollar value of shares repurchased since the beginning of the year to about $2.2 billion from $2.0 billion at the end of the second quarter.

He declined to say when GM's board of directors would revisit the issue of further stock repurchases. GM spent about $469 million during the second quarter to buy back 8.3 million shares of the company's $1-2/3 par-value common stock.

Losh also said GM would end the 1997 calendar year with an increase in U.S. car and truck market share over 1996, but declined to offer a specific target. GM's market share in 1996 declined to 31 percent, and that figure fell again to 30.4 percent for the first six months of 1997.
"We expect to pick up share and we expect to continue to deliver cost savings," Losh said.
He added that cost savings played a significant role in allowing GM to beat the Wall Street consensus with second quarter operating earnings of $2.21 a share. The First Call consensus was $2.10.
Losh said a combination of purchasing cost reductions, savings associated with new models and engineering efficiencies helped to boost GM's results.
